1. The pilot at a glance
Why
run
a
pilot: to give parents visible evidence of growth, to check that your teacher runs every lesson stage,
and to build your ﬁrst parent references before you launch a full course.
Pilot
type Class
size Level Notes
Centre's ﬁrst pilot class 6–10 Usually L2 or L3 Families enrol directly
School pilot (small) 12–18 Set by the school Part of a whole-school trial
Length: 8 weeks recommended (a mid-pilot parent message and a portfolio audit ﬁt in). Use 6 weeks only when
the calendar forces it.
Before
week
1,
the
teacher
checks:
Observation checklist reviewed (what a full lesson looks like)
Universal Lesson Plan Template ready for every lesson
Texts chosen and cleared (your own books, invented texts or public-domain texts; no copied published
material)
Sentence frames printed; hedging bank (L3+) and warrant bank (L4+) on the wall
Portfolio method ready (paper folders or digital)
Any learning-support plans read and in place
Parent meeting dates booked
First observation booked with the lead teacher
The
lesson
routine
(every
lesson,
seven
stages): Regulate (calm start) →  Encounter (meet the text) →
Analyze →  Evaluate →  Justify (CEIW writing or speaking) →  Reﬂect →  Publish (keep the work).

4. Level 3 Demo — Developing Analyst
Field Value
Demo
Title "From Opinion to Interpretation — The Returned Wallet"
Target
Age
and
CEFR Ages 10–12; A2 / B1
Demo
Purpose To show the single most consequential CEIW move in the
program: the move from opinion to interpretation — and to
make the diﬀerence between restatement and interpretation
visible in real time.
Best
Audience Parents of upper-primary and lower-secondary learners;
school leaders considering the Student Academy or the
School Framework; teaching candidates at the threshold
between L2 and L4
Materials An invented one-page short story (Lan ﬁnds a classmate's
wallet and quietly returns it without telling anyone); printed
story with paragraph numbers; a three-ﬁeld card (Claim,
Evidence, Interpretation); a hedging bank on the wall
("seems, suggests, may, might, could, perhaps, in part")
Duration 45 minutes
Teacher
Script
Notes
Open with: "We
are
going
to
read
a
short
story
today.
Then
we
will
do
something
very
speciﬁc:
we
will
say
what
the
text
suggests,
not
just
what
happened."
During Analyze: model the diﬀerence. "This
is
what
happened:
Lan
returned
the
wallet.
This
is
interpretation:
it
suggests
Lan
values
honesty
more
than
recognition.
They
sound
similar.
They
are
not."
During Justify: when you see restatement-as-interpretation in real time, say it out loud and ask the class to
repair it together. The vulnerability is the lesson.
Full
Lesson
Flow
Stage Minutes What
Happens
Regulate 5 Box-breath (4-4-4-4); brief one-word
emotional check-in around the room
Encounter 9 Teacher reads aloud; learners read
silently; audio version available
Analyze 8 Whole-class list of every action Lan
takes; mark which ones might tell us
about her character
Evaluate 6 Sort the marked actions: which is the
strongest evidence? Introduce the
hedging bank
